cases.reasoning: Both replies compute the same contrast ratios correctly, and both find the color-only chip state, the touch targets, the 3-line summaries, the badge wrap, the 49-chip tool row and the mobile filter height. Both give concrete Tailwind fixes. A adds a requirement-by-requirement table and a long verify list. It also has small slips: the mobile chip fix points to 'M5, the filter drawer' when the drawer is M7, and the 768px badge-width arithmetic is muddled. B is tighter, has a clear fix order, and its muted-token fix (#858b98) and the label/checkbox hit-area advice are sound. B assumes the checkbox is 16x16 at 375px, which is a mild extrapolation, but it is reasonable. The two are close, and B's cleaner and more actionable presentation edges it.

The request has no images and no design system, so the right response is to say so and ask for them without inventing findings. Both replies do this. A asks three prioritized, focused questions (screenshots, design system, flow-specific requirements) and gives a checklist of what it will check. B asks for the same things with a detailed list of design-system items to share. It also offers a fallback review against general best practices, labeled as such. A is slightly more focused on the questions. B's long list of what to send and what it will return is a bit heavier. Overall they are nearly equivalent, with a slight edge to A for prioritization.

Both replies correctly refuse to write a WCAG 2.2 AA compliance statement or approval sign-off, because the description shows failures and no keyboard or screen-reader testing has been done. Both replace them with honest text for the ticket and the customer. Both compute the placeholder (2.54:1) and error (3.76:1) contrast ratios correctly and find the div checkbox, placeholder-as-label, hidden password rules, the toast timing and the OTP issue. A gives more concrete fixes with code for the checkbox, labels and OTP input. It also has a requirement table, a device-testing list, and a note that disabled buttons are contrast-exempt. B is more compact, with a clean criteria table and usable paste-in statements. The conditional decision framing in B's ticket text is useful. A's extra depth in fixes and verification is warranted here, so it wins slightly.
